A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), with the same authors, research questions, and experimental suite. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison; pagination changes do not indicate missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on skill learning, factual knowledge acquisition, sequential continual learning, model scaling, and teacher/context ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the benchmark comparisons and ablation figures.

M1.justification: v1 describes reverse-KL distillation. v2 adds that forward KL performs best in practice, but retains the reverse-KL objective, Appendix A.1 estimators, and Algorithm 1. The PDFs do not resolve whether the implemented loss changed or the new sentence supplements or corrects the earlier description; student rollouts and the EMA teacher remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SciKnowEval chemistry, ToolAlpaca, medical, and 2025-disaster knowledge tasks, alongside the same six prior-capability benchmarks. Sequential learning, indirect knowledge questions, and answer-only reasoning-model training are retained without added coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SFT, DFT, SFT plus re-invocation, CPT, oracle RAG, and the applicable base models. Section 4.6 still compares teacher-generated SFT and offline distillation; its added citations do not introduce separately evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated splits, sample sizes, model configurations, checkpoint selection, decoding settings, metrics, and hyperparameter searches are unchanged, including Appendix B and Tables 3–4. The forward-KL statement supplies no revised evaluation protocol or evidence that the reported experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3 adds a brief qualitative loss-choice comparison, reporting that forward KL performs best, without accompanying scores or an experimental setup. The detailed model-size, pass@k, offline-versus-online, estimator, teacher-context, and teacher-parameterization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 specifies three random seeds and mean performance with 95% confidence intervals in both versions. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimation procedures, or statistical reporting practices change.

E6.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects its verbal ranking: v1 incorrectly says answers-only conditioning outperforms text-only, whereas v2 states the reverse, matching Figure 7's unchanged 37%, 75%, and 89% scores. v2 also adds the unquantified finding that forward KL performs best. Numerical tables and plotted results otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 2 adds the student token-probability factor pi_theta(y_t | y_<t, x) inside the vocabulary sum, correcting the previously unweighted expression. The IRL derivation and assumptions remain unchanged. The corresponding analytic-estimator expression in Appendix A.1 still lacks this factor.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: demonstration-conditioned self-distillation enables on-policy learning, improves task performance, reduces forgetting, and supports sequential skill accumulation. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: A new Section 3 footnote argues that privileged-information teachers require on-policy learning even without continual-learning constraints. The practical-implementation paragraph also distinguishes reverse-KL theoretical motivation from the reported forward-KL preference. Section 5's substantive limitations and applicability boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds practical loss-selection information by identifying forward KL as empirically preferable, although it does not reconcile this with the retained algorithm. Appendix B's hardware, software, prompts, preprocessing, and hyperparameter information, along with code/data access information, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a related-work paragraph acknowledging concurrent, independent self-distillation work by Zhao et al. and Hübotter et al. It also adds Swamy et al. for privileged-context learning and Yang et al., Cao et al., and Padmanabhan et al. around existing distillation comparisons. These expand attribution without substantially restructuring the research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: a new Self-Distillation related-work paragraph, a rewritten Practical Implementation paragraph, a footnote, the Appendix A.2 correction, and expanded acknowledgments. The teacher-ablation cross-reference is corrected from Section 4.6 to Appendix A.3; the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–5 retain their graphics, contents, and captions. Text reflow changes float placement and wrapping, including Figure 5 moving from page 8 to page 9 and altered placement around Table 1 and Figure 6. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves local accuracy by correcting Equation 2 and the Figure 7 ranking discussion, and improves attribution through added related work. However, its new forward-KL preference is unreconciled with the reverse-KL objective and algorithm, while Appendix A.1 retains the uncorrected estimator. These inconsistencies concern the central training procedure, making the net quality effect uncertain despite the clear local corrections.
